title: Detect an independently verifiable extraterrestrial technology

concept.text: The innovation would be an independently verifiable discovery of a signal or artifact made by technology of extraterrestrial origin. A technosignature is evidence of technology: detecting one need not involve receiving an intentional message, decoding information or contacting its makers. Breakthrough Listen’s stated search for signs of extraterrestrial technology provides a concrete example of this scientific goal.

Conceptual clarification: the essential requirement is extraterrestrial technological provenance. Showing that something is located beyond Earth would not suffice, because human spacecraft and transmissions also operate in space. A convincing discovery would need evidence that the phenomenon is technological and that its origin cannot credibly be attributed to human activity. The concept includes possible signals and artifacts beyond the radio candidates illustrated by the supplied source.

significance.text: Conditional scientific implication: a verified discovery would establish that technology arose beyond Earth. It would turn the existence of extraterrestrial technology from an open possibility into an observational result, giving astronomy and research on life and intelligence a new empirical starting point. The significance follows from what the proposed discovery would establish; the supplied evidence does not report that this discovery has occurred.

Conditional downstream possibilities would depend on the evidence available. A well-localized source could motivate targeted observations of its environment, while a sufficiently informative signal or artifact might permit investigation of its operation, history or makers. Those possibilities are additional research opportunities, not guaranteed consequences. A detection would not by itself establish that the makers still exist, that the technology remains active, that it represents a whole civilization or that communication is feasible. Evidence of technology also would not automatically establish life on a particular exoplanet.

missing_breakthrough.text: The missing capability is a convincing attribution of an observed phenomenon to extraterrestrial technology, with enough accessible evidence for independent investigators to check that conclusion. The Proxima Centauri candidate illustrates one central obstacle: apparent association with an astronomical target can survive initial filtering and still be explained by human interference. The supplied release describes checks involving neighboring observations and possible satellite sources, showing why observing in a target’s direction is only an initial clue.

Scientific and engineering synthesis: investigators must connect several distinct findings—where the phenomenon originates, whether the recorded feature is real, whether it requires a technological explanation and whether human technology can account for it. Instrument behavior, calibration errors, intermittent interference and natural astrophysical processes can undermine different parts of that chain. Independent observations must preserve the relevant feature while avoiding shared instrumental or analytical mistakes. For a transient event or a faint artifact, obtaining enough additional evidence may itself be the limiting barrier.

Methodological synthesis: there is no single radio-signal test that can establish the provenance of every possible technosignature. Evidence appropriate to a transmission may differ from evidence appropriate to a physical artifact or another astronomical anomaly. An unexplained feature alone would leave a gap between failing to identify its cause and positively establishing extraterrestrial technology. The required breakthrough includes closing that gap with converging evidence, while acknowledging which alternatives remain viable.

current_state.text: In its release dated 25 October 2021, Breakthrough Initiatives reported the analysis of an intriguing Breakthrough Listen candidate observed in the direction of Proxima Centauri. The analysis suggested that the signal was unlikely to originate in that system and instead favored interference from Earth-based human technology. The particular interference source remained unidentified. That residual uncertainty does not erase the evidence favoring interference, but it means the account should not be described as having conclusively identified the responsible device.

The demonstrated achievement in this example is the investigation and rejection of a promising candidate as evidence for technology in the Proxima Centauri system. It illustrates the difficulty of separating a target-associated radio signal from interference; it does not establish how all possible technosignatures would behave or how they should be tested. The release documents a relevant search and false-positive analysis, not a successful detection of extraterrestrial technology.

Evidence scope: the supplied review assessed a complete, untruncated copy of the news release, with no extraction issues recorded. It did not assess the full underlying research papers. The dated account therefore supports the reported 2021 conclusion at the level of the release, without providing a paper-level assessment here. The supplied freshness record is empty, so these materials cannot establish the field’s status through 1 November 2026 or subsequent developments. The source’s recorded retrieval on 11 November 2026 does not make its scientific account more recent than 2021.

completion_criteria.text: Proposed demonstration: independent observations would establish an astronomical origin and reproduce, or independently corroborate, a feature whose technological explanation is compelling after credible human, instrumental and natural alternatives have been tested. Establishing an astronomical location would be one component of the case; the evidence would also need to establish extraterrestrial technological provenance. A readable message would not be required. These are proposed criteria for this record, not an established protocol prescribed by the supplied release.
completion_criteria.label: Proposed demonstration

completion_criteria.text: Proposed reproducibility requirements: investigators should make the relevant observations, calibration information, processing methods and alternative-explanation tests available for independent scrutiny. Where feasible, separate instruments, observatories and analysis teams should recover the decisive evidence. For a nonrepeating event, independent corroboration or additional physical evidence would need to compensate for the inability to observe the same event again; a single unexplained recording would leave a substantial verification gap.
completion_criteria.label: Proposed reproducibility requirements

completion_criteria.text: Proposed practical boundary: a convincing case should state what has been established about the source, the technological feature and the remaining uncertainties. No numerical confidence threshold is supplied or adopted here. Finite observations can establish the demonstrated breadth of checks and the strength of a particular attribution; they cannot exhaust every imaginable natural or human explanation. Completion would concern a compelling, reproducible discovery of at least one extraterrestrial technology, without implying that every future candidate could be classified or that its makers could be contacted.
completion_criteria.label: Proposed practical boundary

related_concepts.text: Roster-based synthesis: AST-01, “Establish that an exoplanet hosts life,” is the closest overlap because extraterrestrial technology would bear directly on research into life and intelligence. The evidentiary targets remain distinct. Evidence of life need not indicate technology, while a technological signal or artifact need not establish that a particular exoplanet currently hosts life. Its makers could be elsewhere, no longer living or separated from the observed evidence by a long interval.

Roster-based synthesis: AST-08, “Produce resolved surface maps of rocky exoplanets,” could supply environmental context or spatial information useful in investigating a candidate associated with a planet. A resolved map would not automatically reveal technology, and AST-02 does not require a planetary surface map. Each concept retains its own completion requirement.

Roster-based synthesis: AST-09, “Make neutrino astronomy capable of routinely resolving hidden cosmic sources,” and AST-10, “Open the millihertz gravitational-wave sky as a working observatory,” overlap methodologically through source localization, instrument validation and separation of signals from backgrounds. Their goals concern observational capabilities for cosmic sources; neither capability would itself establish extraterrestrial technology. AST-02 is defined by the provenance and interpretation of the discovery rather than by opening a particular observing channel.

Roster-based synthesis: AST-03 through AST-07 and AST-11 through AST-14 address other physical constituents, cosmic histories, backgrounds or astrophysical mechanisms. Their relevant connection is the shared need to distinguish a new interpretation from instrumental effects and competing physical explanations. The supplied materials establish no specific dependency between those discoveries and AST-02, so they remain separate innovations.

change_log.change: Replaced location beyond Earth as the decisive requirement with extraterrestrial technological provenance.
change_log.reason: Human spacecraft and transmissions can be beyond Earth; location alone cannot establish the concept’s intended discovery.

change_log.change: Expanded the explanation of technosignatures while preserving signals, artifacts and possibilities beyond radio searches.
change_log.reason: The supplied radio example illustrates a verification problem without defining the full scope of the innovation.

change_log.change: Integrated the dated Proxima Centauri candidate analysis and preserved uncertainty about the specific interference source.
change_log.reason: The release favors terrestrial interference but does not identify the responsible device; neither certainty nor complete agnosticism would accurately represent that finding.

change_log.change: Separated reported achievements from conditional significance, methodological synthesis and proposed completion criteria.
change_log.reason: The supplied evidence documents a search and false-positive investigation, while the breakthrough and its consequences remain hypothetical.

change_log.change: Preserved the limits concerning surviving makers, communication and life on a particular planet.
change_log.reason: Those conclusions require additional evidence beyond detecting extraterrestrial technology.

change_log.change: Added source-scope and freshness limits, including the distinction between the complete release and the unassessed underlying papers.
change_log.reason: Complete extraction of a 2021 announcement does not establish paper-level verification or the field’s status in November 2026.

change_log.change: Developed proposed verification requirements and roster relationships as explicitly labeled synthesis.
change_log.reason: These details make the record usable without attributing a comprehensive protocol or unsupported cross-concept dependencies to the single supplied source.

unresolved_issues: The supplied materials do not establish whether later work changed the interpretation of this candidate or produced other relevant detections through November 2026.
The specific terrestrial interference source favored in the Proxima Centauri candidate analysis remained unidentified in the supplied account.
The underlying research papers were not assessed in the supplied review, leaving their detailed methods and evidentiary strength outside this record’s verified scope.
The appropriate verification tests would depend on the kind of signal or artifact discovered; the supplied materials do not establish a universal protocol or numerical acceptance threshold.
